claims.statement: Genomic classifications change, laboratories need documented reevaluation workflows, and professional reanalysis services may justifiably be billable.
Laboratory burden is real: a study covering all nine Dutch diagnostic laboratories found reactive practice common and routine periodic reinterpretation viewed as infeasible.
Recontact is professionally desirable in selected cases but responsibility and a universal duty remain unsettled.
An autonomous NGS interpretation or diagnostic-decision product would enter IVD medical-device scope under current EU guidance.
The registry would process genetic special-category data and therefore needs a complete GDPR basis, safeguards, minimization, and security design.
EHDS genomic and second-wave lab-result milestones are mainly 2031 and do not prove near-term buying urgency.
SeqOne already markets automatic monthly historical-case reevaluation, creating direct incumbent pressure on the original automation layer.
Polish providers currently charge for reanalysis, proving a paid clinical event but not an annual software subscription.
ClinVar offers a free, weekly-updated classification comparison source, while patient identity, consent, clinical review, and recontact remain outside that public database.
A vendor-neutral lab-owned administrative workflow is a more plausible wedge than duplicating clinical interpretation, provided intended-purpose counsel agrees.
No reviewed source establishes laboratory commitment, eligible imported-record volume, annual per-record willingness to pay, or a non-IVD classification for the exact product.

contrary_evidence: c705-s7 is a direct automated-reevaluation incumbent.
c705-s8 through c705-s10 show laboratories already own paid reanalysis services.
c705-s2 documents operational resistance to routine periodic reinterpretation.
c705-s4 creates a material regulatory boundary around any clinical interpretation feature.
c705-s6 does not create near-term demand, and c705-s11 commoditizes the public update feed.
